To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a standardized chelating protocol by stratifying thalassemics into well, poorly and risk chelation groups according to their SF levels and T2* values is safe and efficacious.

the combined use of DFO and L1 was the only regimen that could significantly reduce iron overload in thalassemics with cardiac complications, and this regimen was safe and well-tolerated in this patient population.
the combined use of L1 and DFX in thalassemics is safe and efficacious, and that the use of L1 alone is not recommended.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to stratification of thalassemias patients based on SF and MRI cardiac T2* values.
the use of stratification based on SF levels and MRI T2* measurements to guide thalassemics towards a personalized and effective chelation regimen.
a practical chelation protocol based on stratification of transfusion-dependent thallasemic patients by SF and MRI cardiac T2* measurement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combined therapy with L and DFO (III) is superior to the monotherapy with L (II) in reducing cardiac iron overload in thalassemics with high SF levels (Group C) but the monotherapy with DFO (I) is sufficient in patients with low SF levels (Group A) and in thalassecimics with high SF and low T2* (Group B).
the combined therapy (L1 + DFO) is superior to DFO alone or L1 alone in the management of iron overload in thalassemics with cardiac complications.
combined therapy of DFO with L1 was effective and safe in improving iron overload status in thalassemics with cardiac risk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combined therapy with DFO and L1 is the most effective chelation regimen for thalassemics with cardiac iron overload.
a practical chelation strategy based on stratification of thalassemics by their SF levels and MRI cardiac T2* is effective in reducing their iron overload.
combined therapy with L and DFO is safe and effective in reducing iron overload, especially for those with risk of cardiac complications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stratification of thalassemics by their SF and cardiac T2* levels is useful in determining their iron overload and the type of chelation therapy to be given.

a stratification approach based on SF levels and MRI T2* measurements is effective in identifying thalassemics with cardiac complications and in tailoring chelation protocols to improve iron overload status.
a practical chelation protocol based on stratification of thalassemics by serum ferritin levels and cardiac MRI T2* measurement is feasible in a resource-poor setting.
